options.why: This adds F(a) instead of subtracting it.
Correct. An antiderivative is $$F(x) = -x^{3} - 2x^{2} - 5x$$; $$F(4) - F(1) = -108$$.
This is F(b) only; subtract F(a) as well.
This subtracts values of the integrand instead of an antiderivative.

questions.explanation: By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, $$\int_{1}^{4} f(x)\,dx = F(4) - F(1)$$ with $$F(x) = -x^{3} - 2x^{2} - 5x$$. That is $$-116 - (-8) = -108$$.

questions.stem: Based on the table, which of the following is the best estimate of $$\lim_{x \to -1} f(x)$$?

options.why: Averaging the two sides is never how a limit is found.
This is only the left-hand trend.
This is only the right-hand trend.
Correct. From the left the outputs approach 5; from the right they approach 8. The one-sided limits differ.

questions.explanation: Read the table toward $$x = -1$$ from each side. The left side approaches 5 and the right side approaches 8, so the two-sided limit does not exist.

questions.stem: A population $$P$$ grows according to $$\frac{dP}{dt} = kP$$, and it doubles every 2 years. If $$P(0) = 200$$, what is $$P(6)$$?

options.why: Correct. $$6$$ years is 3 doubling periods, so the population is multiplied by $$2^{3}$$.
This adds the original amount once per period (linear growth); exponential growth multiplies by 2 each period.
This counts only one doubling period.
This treats each year as a doubling period.

questions.stem: The functions $$f$$, $$g$$, and $$h$$ satisfy $$g(x) \leq f(x) \leq h(x)$$ for all $$x$$, where $$g(x) = 6 - 3(x - 1)^2$$ and $$h(x) = 6 + 3(x - 1)^2$$. What is $$\lim_{x \to 1} f(x)$$?

options.why: This adds the limits of $$g$$ and $$h$$; the squeeze gives their common value.
Correct. Both $$g$$ and $$h$$ approach $$6$$ as $$x \to 1$$, so the Squeeze Theorem forces $$f$$ to approach $$6$$ too.

options.text: It cannot be determined without a formula for $$f$$.
options.why: The Squeeze Theorem determines the limit without a formula for $$f$$, because the bounds share the same limit.
This is the input value being approached, not the output.

questions.explanation: $$\lim_{x \to 1} g(x) = 6$$ and $$\lim_{x \to 1} h(x) = 6$$. Since $$f$$ is trapped between them, the Squeeze Theorem gives $$\lim_{x \to 1} f(x) = 6$$.

questions.stem: A particle moves along the x-axis so that its position at time $$t \geq 0$$ is $$x(t) = t^{3} - 21t^{2} + 120t$$. At what times is the particle at rest?

options.why: At $$t = 0$$ the position is 0, but the velocity is $$120$$, so the particle is moving.
This is where the acceleration is zero, not the velocity.
This is where the position is zero, not the velocity.
Correct. $$v(t) = 3t^2 - 42t + 120 = 3(t - 4)(t - 10)$$, which is zero at $$t = 4$$ and $$t = 10$$.

questions.explanation: The particle is at rest when $$v(t) = x'(t) = 0$$. $$v(t) = 3(t - 4)(t - 10)$$, so $$t = 4$$ and $$t = 10$$.

questions.stem: The function $$f$$ is differentiable with $$f(1) = 6$$ and $$f'(1) = -2$$. Using the tangent line to the graph of $$f$$ at $$x = 1$$, what is the approximation of $$f(1.3)$$?

options.why: Sign error in the change in x.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = \begin{cases} 3x - 5 & x < 0 \\ 4x + 5 & x \geq 0 \end{cases}$$. What is $$\lim_{x \to 0} f(x)$$?

options.why: Correct. The left-hand limit is $$-5$$ and the right-hand limit is $$5$$. They differ, so the two-sided limit does not exist.
This is the left-hand limit only. The right-hand limit is $$5$$.
This is $$f(0)$$ and the right-hand limit only. The left-hand limit is $$-5$$.
A limit is never the average of the one-sided limits. When they differ, the limit does not exist.

questions.explanation: From the left, $$f(x) = 3x - 5 \to -5$$. From the right, $$f(x) = 4x + 5 \to 5$$. Since $$-5 \neq 5$$, $$\lim_{x \to 0} f(x)$$ does not exist.

questions.stem: At what value of $$x$$ does the graph of $$f(x) = -x^{3} - 6x^{2} + 4x - 1$$ have a point of inflection?

options.why: This is −b/(2a), the vertex formula for a parabola, applied to the cubic's coefficients. Set f″(x) = 0 instead.
Correct. $$f''(x) = -6x - 12$$ is zero and changes sign at $$x = -2$$.
Sign error when solving f″(x) = 0.
Inflection points are where f″ changes sign, not where f″ has its constant term.

questions.explanation: $$f'(x) = -3x^{2} - 12x + 4$$ and $$f''(x) = -6x - 12$$. $$f''$$ is linear, so it changes sign at its zero, $$x = -2$$.

This is the value of the function, not its derivative.

questions.stem: A farmer has 112 meters of fencing to enclose a rectangular field along a straight river. No fence is needed along the river. What is the largest possible area of the field, in square meters?

options.why: This makes all three fenced sides equal, which is not optimal.
Correct. With width $$x$$ perpendicular to the river, $$A = x(112 - 2x)$$, maximized at $$x = 28$$.
This fences all four sides (a square), but the river side needs no fence.
This doesn't account for the two equal sides perpendicular to the river.

questions.explanation: $$A(x) = x(112 - 2x)$$, $$A'(x) = 112 - 4x = 0$$ at $$x = 28$$, and $$A'' = -4 < 0$$, so this is a maximum. The dimensions are $$28$$ by $$56$$, with area $$1568$$.

questions.stem: A particle moves along a line with velocity $$v(t) = 3(t - 3)(t - 7)$$ for $$t \geq 0$$. For which values of $$t$$ is the particle speeding up?

options.why: This misses $$3 < t < 5$$, where both $$v$$ and $$a$$ are negative.
This is where the velocity is negative, which only means the particle moves left.
Correct. The particle speeds up when velocity and acceleration have the same sign.
On $$0 < t < 3$$ the velocity is positive but the acceleration is negative, so it is slowing down.

questions.explanation: $$a(t) = 6t - 30$$ changes sign at $$t = 5$$. $$v$$ is negative on $$(3, 7)$$ and positive elsewhere. Both are negative on $$(3, 5)$$ and both positive for $$t > 7$$.

questions.stem: If $$f(x) = \arcsin\left(\frac{x}{13}\right)$$, what is $$f'(5)$$?

options.why: The derivative of arcsine is positive; this has a sign error.

questions.stem: What is $$\lim_{x \to -2} \frac{x^{2} + 8x + 12}{x + 2}$$?

options.why: The expression is undefined at the point, but its outputs nearby approach a single number, so the limit exists.

questions.explanation: Direct substitution gives $$\frac{0}{0}$$, so factor: $$x^{2} + 8x + 12 = (x + 2)(x + 6)$$. For $$x \neq -2$$ the expression equals $$x + 6$$, so the limit is $$-2 - (-6) = 4$$.

questions.stem: Using a left Riemann sum with the four subintervals indicated by the table, what is the approximation of $$\int_0^{10} R(t)\,dt$$?

questions.stem: If $$f(x) = \csc x$$, what is $$f'\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)$$?

options.why: This mixes up the derivative with a different trigonometric value at the point.
Correct. $$f'(x) = -\csc x \cot x$$, evaluated at $$\frac{\pi}{6}$$.

questions.stem: Let $$g(x) = \int_0^{x} f(t)\,dt$$. What is $$g(3)$$?

options.why: Sign error: area above the axis counts positive.

questions.stem: The derivative of a function $$f$$ is $$f'(x) = (x - 1)^2(x - 3)$$. On which intervals is $$f$$ increasing?

questions.stem: The region enclosed by $$y = x$$ and $$y = x^2$$ is revolved about the x-axis. What is the volume of the resulting solid?

questions.stem: Consider the curve $$x^2 - xy + y^2 = 3$$, for which $$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{y - 2x}{2y - x}$$. At which points on the curve is the tangent line horizontal?

These points do not lie on the curve.

questions.stem: Let $$R$$ be the region bounded by $$y = x^2$$ and $$y = 1$$. Which of the following gives the volume of the solid generated when $$R$$ is revolved about the line $$y = 1$$?

options.why: This uses the distance from the curve to the x-axis, not to the line of revolution.
Correct. Each disc has radius $$1 - x^2$$, the distance from the curve to the axis.

The radius must be squared, and the region runs from −k to k.

questions.explanation: Revolving about $$y = 1$$, which is the top boundary, gives discs of radius $$1 - x^2$$.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = 2x^{3} + 6x^{2} - 18x$$. At what value of $$x$$ does $$f$$ have a relative minimum?

questions.stem: Using the data in the table and the values on either side of $$x = 4$$, what is the best estimate of $$g'(4)$$?

questions.stem: Which of the following is the solution to $$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{x}{y}$$ with $$y(0) = 5$$?

options.why: This would have dy/dx = 1, which is not x/y.
Correct. $$y\,dy = x\,dx$$ gives $$y^2 = x^2 + C$$; $$C = 25$$, and the positive root matches $$y(0) = 5$$.

questions.stem: What is the absolute maximum value of $$f(x) = x^2e^{-x/2} + \frac{\sin x}{4}$$ on the interval $$[0, 9]$$?

questions.stem: The function $$g$$ is defined by $$g(x) = \frac{\sin(2x)}{e^{6x} - 1}$$ for $$x \neq 0$$. For what value of $$g(0)$$ is $$g$$ continuous at $$x = 0$$?

options.why: The two small quantities do not shrink at the same rate.

Correct. Evaluating $$g$$ at inputs very close to 0 (or using the limits of $$\frac{\sin u}{u}$$ and $$\frac{e^u - 1}{u}$$) gives $$\frac{2}{6}$$.

questions.explanation: For continuity, $$g(0)$$ must equal $$\lim_{x \to 0} g(x)$$. Near 0, $$\sin(2x) \approx 2x$$ and $$e^{6x} - 1 \approx 6x$$, so the limit is $$\frac{2}{6} \approx 0.333$$. A table of values near 0 confirms it.

questions.stem: Sand is added to a pile at a rate modeled by $$R(t) = 11 + 4\sin\left(\frac{t}{4}\right)\sqrt{t + 1}$$ cubic feet per hour, for $$0 \leq t \leq 8$$. At time $$t = 0$$ the pile contains 263 cubic feet of sand. How much sand is in the pile at $$t = 8$$?

Correct. $$263 + \int_0^{8} R(t)\,dt$$.

questions.explanation: Amount = initial amount + accumulated change = $$263 + \int_0^{8} R(t)\,dt \approx 263 + 142.281 = 405.281$$ cubic feet.

questions.stem: A particle moves along a line with velocity $$v(t) = 3\sin(t)\,e^{-t/6} + 0.3$$. What is the total distance the particle travels over $$0 \leq t \leq 4$$?

options.why: This is the speed at the final time.

questions.explanation: Total distance $$= \int_0^{4} |v(t)|\,dt \approx 5.945$$. The displacement $$\int_0^{4} v(t)\,dt \approx 5.288$$ is smaller because the particle moves backward part of the time.

questions.stem: The temperature of a room, in degrees Fahrenheit, is modeled by $$H(t) = 89 + 18\sin\left(\frac{t}{8}\right)e^{-t/20}$$, where $$t$$ is measured in hours. What is the instantaneous rate of change of the temperature at $$t = 10$$, in degrees Fahrenheit per hour?

questions.explanation: The instantaneous rate of change is $$H'(10) \approx -0.088$$ degrees Fahrenheit per hour, from the calculator's numerical derivative.

questions.stem: The derivative of a function $$f$$ is $$f'(x) = \sin\left(\frac{x^2}{4}\right) - 0.50\cos x$$. How many relative extrema does $$f$$ have on the open interval $$0 < x < 4$$?

questions.stem: Let $$R$$ be the region bounded by $$y = \sqrt{x}\,e^{-x/4} + 0.2$$, the x-axis, $$x = 0$$, and $$x = 4$$. What is the volume of the solid generated when $$R$$ is revolved about the line $$y = -1$$?

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = x^{3} + 3x + e^{x/2}$$, and let $$g$$ be the inverse of $$f$$. What is the value of $$g'(6)$$?

options.why: This is f′ at the matching input; the inverse's derivative is its reciprocal.
This evaluates $$f'$$ at $$6$$ instead of at the input where $$f(x) = 6$$.
Correct. Solve $$f(x) = 6$$ to get $$x \approx 1.050$$, then $$g'(6) = \frac{1}{f'(1.050)}$$.

questions.explanation: Use the calculator to solve $$f(x) = 6$$: $$x \approx 1.050$$, so $$g(6) \approx 1.050$$. Then $$g'(6) = \frac{1}{f'(g(6))} \approx \frac{1}{7.155} \approx 0.140$$.

parts.prompt: How many gallons of water enter the tank during the time interval $$0 \leq t \leq 8$$?

rubric.criterion: Writes a definite integral of $$E$$ over the interval.
Gives the correct value.

parts.prompt: Is the amount of water in the tank increasing or decreasing at time $$t = 3$$? Give a reason for your answer.

rubric.criterion: Concludes correctly, with a reason that compares $$E$$ and $$L$$ (or uses the sign of $$E - L$$).
rubric.example: $$E(3) - L(3) \approx 7.985$$, which is positive, so the amount is increasing.

parts.prompt: At what time $$t$$, for $$0 \leq t \leq 8$$, is the amount of water in the tank greatest? Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Sets $$E(t) - L(t) = 0$$ to find the critical points.
Evaluates the amount at the critical points and the endpoints (Candidates Test).
Gives the correct time with justification.

parts.prompt: How many gallons of water are in the tank at time $$t = 8$$?

rubric.criterion: Uses the initial amount plus the integral of the net rate.
Gives the correct value.

parts.prompt: Find the acceleration of the particle at time $$t = 3.5$$. Is the speed of the particle increasing or decreasing at that time? Give a reason.

rubric.criterion: Gives the correct acceleration.
Concludes about the speed by comparing the signs of velocity and acceleration.
rubric.example: $$v(3.5) \approx 2.051$$. Velocity and acceleration have opposite signs, so the speed is decreasing.

parts.prompt: Find the position of the particle at time $$t = 4$$.

rubric.criterion: Uses the initial position plus the integral of velocity.
Gives the correct position.

parts.prompt: Find the total distance traveled by the particle over $$0 \leq t \leq 4$$.

rubric.criterion: Integrates the absolute value of velocity (or splits at the sign changes).
Gives the correct distance.

parts.prompt: At what times in the interval $$0 < t < 4$$ does the particle change direction? Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the times where $$v$$ changes sign, with justification.
rubric.example: $$v(t)$$ changes sign at $$t \approx 0.792$$ and $$t \approx 3.883$$, so the particle changes direction there.

parts.prompt: Find $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}$$ in terms of $$x$$ and $$y$$. Is the approximation in part (b) an overestimate or an underestimate? Explain.

rubric.criterion: Finds the second derivative.
Uses the sign of the second derivative at the point to conclude.
rubric.example: At $$(1, -3)$$, $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -60$$, so f is concave down and the tangent line lies above the curve: an overestimate.

parts.prompt: Use a trapezoidal sum with the four subintervals shown in the table to approximate $$\int_0^{12} P(t)\,dt$$. Explain the meaning of this integral in the context of the problem.

rubric.criterion: Sets up the trapezoidal sum with unequal widths.
Gives the correct value.
Interprets the integral with units.
rubric.example: The total number of people who enter the park during the first 12 minutes.

parts.prompt: Must there be a time $$c$$, for $$3 < c < 9$$, such that $$P'(c) = 0$$? Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Answers yes, citing the Mean Value Theorem (or Rolle's Theorem) with its conditions.
rubric.example: Yes. $$P$$ is differentiable (so continuous), and $$P(3) = P(9) = 75$$. By the Mean Value Theorem there is a $$c$$ with $$P'(c) = \frac{75 - 75}{6} = 0$$.

parts.prompt: Must there be a time $$t$$, for $$0 < t < 3$$, at which $$P(t) = 70$$? Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Answers yes, citing the Intermediate Value Theorem and continuity.
rubric.example: Yes. $$P$$ is continuous, and $$70$$ is between $$P(0) = 20$$ and $$P(3) = 75$$, so the IVT guarantees such a $$t$$.

parts.prompt: Find the x-coordinates of all relative extrema of $$f$$, and classify each as a relative maximum or relative minimum. Justify your answer.

rubric.example: $$f'$$ changes from positive to negative at $$-1$$ (relative maximum) and from negative to positive at $$2$$ (relative minimum).

parts.prompt: On what intervals is the graph of $$f$$ concave down? Give a reason.
